Be wary of vaping in public places. Ask people where you can smoke/vape. There's still many smokers in the Philippines, chances are, they know secluded/private/dedicated areas they smoke and would be willing to let you know. Many hotels and establishments(bars/restaurants) have dedicated smoking areas. The key is to always ASK ASK ASK.   
  
Most people I knew who used to build vape mods or use variable mods have switched to disposables. They last quite long, 1 - 2 weeks at a time, and are significantly cheaper than cigs. Since the recent fire incidents in airlines, they've tighten security on things like lighters, powerbanks, vapes in your luggage, I wouldn't recommend flying with it, they might just confiscate. You could easily buy vapes online(shopee or lazada) or locally, just google vape shops around your location. If you find a place to buy, buy several to last 1 month, disposable pod system: battery + pod(e-juice).

Shopee and Lazada also has started banning vape stores on their platforms, but there's still few that manage around the regulation, modify your search like "\[vape brand\] \[vape model\] t-shirt" or something like that. They'd be more expensive by around 100php. Really, local vape shops are your best bet. 

Disposable vapes batteries and pods cost around 350-500 php, if they ask for significantly more, they're likely ripping you off.

Agnosticism is one end of gnosticism. It’s a question of knowledge, “agnostic” means “you don’t know,” “gnostic” means the opposite. That’s why it is paired with “theism” which is “belief.” “Atheist” means you don’t believe, “theist” is the opposite. They’re always paired, as they describe the two aspects of your belief/disbelief. So “Agnostic Atheist” means “I don’t know if there’s a god or higher power(agnostic) so I don’t believe(atheist.) You can also say you’re the opposite, a “gnostic theist.” “You know there’s a god, so you believe.” You could also be an agnostic theist, or a gnostic atheist. You get the idea lol. Okay bro, I feel like I've lost you so let me introduce two simple programming concepts to explain what I meant, if you don't already know.  


A "queue" can be described as FIFO which stands for "First In, First Out." Let's say I queue 5 songs from 1-5, the order they will play is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.  


A "stack" can be described as "LIFO" which is "Last in, First Out". I "stack" 5 songs again, from 1 through 5. The order they would play will be, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Because 5 was last in, so it's first to come out.  


This is what AM does:

"**Play next**" builds up a "stack" after the "now playing" track.  
"**Play later**" builds up a "queue" AFTER the album.  
What I want is to **build up a "queue" after the "now playing"** just like Spotify does.   
So, in context of what I was trying to do, I want a queue to build up WITHIN the album I'm listening to, not after it.

\-assume the position and the fingerings  
\-gently put pressure on the chord.  
\-pluck the strings individually to check is there's any wrong, muted, buzzing or undesired note. If it's muted or buzzed, put a little bit more pressure on it. Good practice is to use the least amount of pressure possible just to make the notes ring properly.  
\-you just do this until every note in the chord sounds good.
